chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Yaqoub al-Hashimi, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of befriending the fool, for the closer you get to him (for his pleasure), the closer you are to your misfortune.'

key_terms.الْأَحْمَقِ: The fool / the one lacking wisdom

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of befriending a foolish person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against the intimacy of the foolish (*al-ahmaq*), noting that their proximity often brings hidden harm closer than expected. This advice reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *mu'asarah* (companionship) as a formative influence, where the intellectual and spiritual deficiencies of a companion can subtly erode one's own state. The warning underscores the practical necessity of discerning friendship to preserve one's religious and social well-being.
